description: The conformance corpus: the fixtures every deadset analyzer passes as a condition of its release. corpus_version is the semantic version of the corpus as one unit, independent of the contract version in contract/contract.json and of this repository's release tags, because the two move for different reasons: the contract moves when a vocabulary or a schema changes, the corpus moves when a fixture is added, which happens each time an analyzer implements a kind. The first published corpus is 1.0.0, and no corpus version is below it, because the fixtures do not change without notice. The major number moves when an existing expectation changes its answer or a format field changes incompatibly, the minor when a fixture or an optional field is added, the patch when only descriptions change. Every analyzer names the corpus version it answers in its conformance report, and a run against a corpus of another major version is not a conformance result.

layout.description: Where the parts of a fixture live. A fixture is one directory under fixtures/, named by the value of its expectation file's name field. It holds exactly one expectation file and one rendering per language the expectation file lists. The Go rendering is one txtar archive whose sections are the files of the rendering, fixture.json among them; the TypeScript rendering is a directory holding the same files. Inside a rendering, the target being analyzed lives under the target directory and each consumer the expectation file names lives in a directory of that name at the rendering root, so a consumer named consumer is target/'s sibling consumer/. A fixture whose setup_failure class is missing-consumer holds no directory for a consumer that member's names lists, and the runner still declares that consumer at the path the directory would have, so the run meets a declared consumer that is absent. Every path in a manifest is relative to the rendering root, which is the archive for Go and the ts/ directory for TypeScript. In a Go rendering each consumer module requires the target module and carries a replace directive naming the target's path relative to the consumer directory, ../target, so the rendering loads with no network access. A Go rendering may also carry a dependency directory: a directory at the rendering root that is neither the target nor a consumer holds a second local module the target's own module file requires and replaces with that directory's path relative to the target, ../<dependency>, so the target resolves the requirement from the rendering rather than from a network. A dependency is named by nothing: the expectation file names its consumers, and every other directory at the rendering root is a dependency, which is what keeps it out of the consumer set the runner loads. A TypeScript rendering may carry an installed directory at the rendering root, holding one directory per installed package, each with its manifest, at the path below node_modules the package's name gives it; the runner renames the directory node_modules in its scratch copy, so the target resolves the installed manifests of its dependencies from the rendering, and the installed directory is neither the target nor a consumer.

schemas.description: The JSON Schema 2020-12 document each fixture file is an instance of, and the two documents an analyzer exchanges with the corpus: the declared gaps it commits and the results its runner writes.

vocabularies.description: The closed vocabularies an expectation file draws a value from, keyed by the expectation-file field that uses each and naming the contract file and the field within it that declares the values. A value outside its vocabulary fails the corpus itself, so an issue kind or an exemption class cannot enter a fixture before it enters the contract.

report.description: The code of a live issue kind, or the literal none for a subject that must not be reported.

retained_by.description: The exemption classes that hold a subject back from being reported.

symbol_kind.description: The kind of subject a reported finding is about, which is what decides whether that finding carries a liveness relation.

details.description: The members a reported finding's details may carry, and the shape of each. The expectation schema names the members the codes carry under the reading a language-neutral expectation can state, so a member whose value is a position or a stable symbol reference is named nowhere in a fixture.

confidence.description: The confidence a reported finding carries, which is its reachability class capped by the kind's maximum class and by the confidence of its component's root members.

reachability_class.description: The reachability class derived from the target kind and the loaded consumers.

notes.description: The kinds of note a run's report may carry, which an entry of the expectation file's notes member names.

setup_failure.description: The classes of setup failure a run may end with, which the expectation file's setup_failure member names.

languages.description: The languages a fixture has a rendering for. This is the one place a fixture names a language; no field of an expectation does.

subject_shapes.description: Which shape each subject of a finding has, drawn from the symbol.kind vocabulary of contract/finding.schema.json, because the shape is what decides whether the suppression phase below applies to an expectation about that subject. A part is a piece of one declaration, judged by no liveness relation of its own and suppressed through the declaration its reference names. A row is a record of a document rather than a thing the program declares, judged by no relation and bound by no suppression, because a suppression record names a declaration. Every other kind is a declaration, suppressed at its own position, and is named by neither list: a kind these lists leave out is one. Every kind the finding schema lists as carrying no liveness relation is named by one of the two lists.

runner.description: What an analyzer does with a fixture, stated so that two analyzers sharing no code answer it the same way.
runner.select: The analyzer answers every fixture whose expectation file lists its language, and only through the rendering for that language. A fixture that lists the language and has no rendering for it fails the corpus, not the analyzer.
runner.load: The analyzer extracts or copies the rendering to a scratch directory, renaming a TypeScript rendering's installed directory node_modules, runs over target/ with the expectation file's target_kind as the configured target kind and each name in consumers as a loaded consumer rooted at the directory of that name, and leaves every file of the rendering byte-identical. It configures no build matrix, so a rendering whose files carry build constraints is analyzed under the matrix the analyzer derives from them; the rendering's manifest declares the identifiers that matrix holds, and an expectation names configurations from that list. It declares the world the expectation file's closed_world member names and nothing further: consumers sets the configuration's consumers.complete, and matrix sets its analysis.matrix.complete together with its analysis.configurations, read from the identifiers the rendering's manifest declares because a matrix a run derived is never a complete one; each key is left at its default where the member does not name the fact, so a fixture that omits the member is analyzed under the open world and a kind whose precondition is a complete world reports nothing. It sets roots.patterns to the entries the expectation file's configured_roots member names and leaves that key at its default where the fixture omits the member, so a fixture that omits it is analyzed under the roots the analysis marks itself. It sets each key the expectation file's configured_declarations member names to the entries the member names under that key, in ascending order of logical name, and leaves every other such key at its default; an entry under ts.lifecycle_contracts.components or ts.lifecycle_contracts.bases is written as one ts.lifecycle_contracts entry of its own, holding that entry alone under the named list and the members the expectation file names for it. It sets analysis.min_confidence to the value the expectation file's min_confidence member names and leaves that key at its default where the fixture omits the member. It sets ts.entry_files to the patterns the expectation file's entry_files member names and ts.disabled_conventions to the row names its disabled_conventions member names, and leaves each key at its default where the fixture omits the member. It leaves the edges document the rendering's target carries, deadset-edges.json, as it is.
runner.resolve: Each expectation's symbol is a fixture-local logical name. The analyzer maps it through the rendering's manifest to a file and a line, and a finding answers the expectation when its position is in that file on that line. A logical name the manifest does not carry, or carries without a file or a line, is a defect in the corpus. A logical name the expectation file's configured_roots member names is a configured root rather than a subject of the rendering: it maps through that member to the entry the runner configures, no rendering's manifest carries it, and a name both documents carry is a defect in the corpus. A logical name the configured_declarations member names is a configured declaration and resolves the same way: it maps through that member to the entry the runner configures, no rendering's manifest carries it, and a name two of the expectation file's members or the member and a manifest both carry is a defect in the corpus. The symbol an edge_evaluations entry names is a logical name of the rendering and resolves through its manifest as an expectation's does, and so does each name the type_error_skips member lists.
runner.report_phase: For an expectation whose report is a code, the analyzer must produce exactly one finding at the resolved position under that code, carrying the confidence the expectation names and, where the expectation names them, the symbol kind, the reachability class, the liveness relation and the configurations the finding holds in. An expectation that names a symbol kind states what the finding's subject is, so the runner reads the rule contract/finding.schema.json states on the liveness relation from it as well. That rule turns on the subject and on the code together: a finding whose subject kind or whose code that rule names must carry no liveness relation, and a finding naming neither must carry one. An expectation that names no symbol kind is answered without that check. Where the expectation names details, each member it names must equal the member of the same name in the finding's own details, compared value by value, and the members it does not name are not compared, so a row pins what it names and nothing further; a member the finding does not carry at all is a mismatch rather than an omission. Where the expectation names component, each member it names must equal the member of the same name in the finding's own component, compared value by value, and the members it does not name are not compared. For an expectation whose report is none, the analyzer must produce no finding at the resolved position; where the expectation names retained_by, the analyzer's retained-symbol listing must name that position with exactly those classes. An expectation whose report is DS1703 is answered from the report's stale_suppressions array rather than from its findings, because a stale suppression is a record of that array and no finding: the analyzer must produce exactly one record whose position resolves to the row's, carrying the mechanism the row's details names, and the row's confidence and symbol kind are answered by the values contract/report.schema.json fixes for the rendering of a record, certain and suppression; such a row names no reachability class, no liveness relation and no configurations, because a record carries none. An expectation whose report is DS1704 is answered by the finding's subject rather than by its position: the analyzer must produce exactly one finding under that code whose subject reference is the configured_roots entry the row's logical name names, wherever the analyzer positions it, because that position is in the configuration document the runner wrote and not in a file of the rendering. An expectation whose logical name names a configured_roots entry and whose report is none states that the entry matched a symbol, so the analyzer must produce no finding under DS1704 naming that entry. An expectation whose report is DS1706 is answered by the finding's subject in the same way: the analyzer must produce exactly one finding under that code whose subject reference is the configured_declarations entry the row's logical name names, spelled as contract/finding.schema.json spells a configured declaration's reference, and whose position is in the configuration document the runner wrote, the line not compared. An expectation whose logical name names a configured_declarations entry and whose report is none states that the entry matched a declaration, so the analyzer must produce no finding under DS1706 naming that entry. An entry of the expectation file's edge_evaluations member is answered from the report's edge_evaluations array: the analyzer must produce exactly one record naming that edge and that side, carrying that state, and for a dead side a finding under the entry's code whose position resolves to the entry's symbol. A finding a record carries is pending and appears nowhere else in the report, so a row whose position is the pending finding's answers as no finding there. Each name of the expectation file's type_error_skips member is answered from the report's type_error_skips array: the analyzer must produce at least one record whose path and line resolve to the name's file and line, the message not compared. Each entry of the expectation file's notes member is answered from the report's notes array: the analyzer must produce exactly one record of that kind and that path, the message not compared. Each entry of the expectation file's conventions_applied member is answered from the report's conventions_applied array: the analyzer must produce exactly one entry of that name, package, version and manifest.
runner.closed_world: The expectation list is exhaustive by position and by code. A finding fails the analyzer unless an expectation resolves to its position and names its code, so a second finding at a position an expectation names under another code fails it, and the corpus pins the absence of a false positive as firmly as the presence of a true one. A record of the report's stale_suppressions array counts as a finding at its own position, and a finding whose subject is a configured root or a configured declaration counts by the entry its subject names rather than by its position, so the two arms the report phase answers from are as exhaustive as the findings array. The edge_evaluations member is exhaustive in the same way: a record of the report's edge_evaluations array that no entry names, by edge and side, fails the analyzer, and a fixture that omits the member expects the array empty. The type_error_skips, notes and conventions_applied members are exhaustive in the same way: a record of the report's type_error_skips array that resolves to no name the member lists, or a record of its notes or conventions_applied array that no entry names, fails the analyzer, and a fixture that omits any of the three members expects that array empty.
runner.setup_failure: A fixture whose expectation file carries setup_failure is answered by the run's end rather than by a report: the analyzer must exit with the failure code contract/exit-codes.json names, report no finding, and print on standard error at least one line that starts with setup failure:, a space, the member's class, a colon and a space, and contains every string of the member's names. Such a fixture has no suppression phase and exercises the member's class as its one capability. A fixture of the class missing-consumer is loaded with every consumer its consumers member names declared at the directory of that name, including the ones the rendering does not hold.
runner.suppression_phase: The phase runs for every expectation whose report is a code about a subject the subject_shapes block above names a declaration or a part of one, and for no other expectation, because contract/grammar/suppression.md binds a record to a declaration: a part is suppressed through the declaration its reference names, and a row reports a record of a document and no declaration, so no record can bind to it and the remedy for such a finding is the change it names or the severity the configuration gives its code. For the expectations the phase applies to, the analyzer writes the reported finding into the rendering's ignore file in the documented form, runs again over the same scratch copy, and must produce no finding at that position and no stale-suppression finding for the entry. Both languages run the same two phases, so a divergence in matching or scoping is a conformance failure.
runner.capabilities: The capabilities an expectation exercises are its report code when that is not none and each class in its retained_by. An analyzer that does not implement one records a declared gap naming the fixture and the capability, and the runner reports the expectation as a gap rather than as a pass or a fail. An expectation with report none and no retained_by exercises no capability and admits no gap. The fixture-level members exercise capabilities of their own: setup_failure its class, type_error_skips the capability type-error-skips, each notes entry its kind, each conventions_applied entry the name of its row, and each disabled_conventions entry the name it disables, so an analyzer whose table carries no row of that name declares a gap naming it.
runner.results: Each fixture ends as pass, gap or fail. An expectation the analyzer neither answers nor declares a gap for is a fail, never a silence.
